segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
In the month of Adar,
there was an overflow of the rivers,
and the river Euphrates rose,
and destroyed a great number of houses in Baghdad.
A certain rich man in Baghdad,
when the water reached his terrace (or upper chamber),
feared lest the house should collapse.
And he prepared two boats,
and filled them with all his possessions, his wives, his children, and his maidservants.
And he commanded the boatmen
to convey them to a high place.
And when they had sailed a little,
one boat sank.
And there were in it nine maidservants of great price,
and one girl of seven years whom her mother had made flee with them {OCR?}.
And they were all drowned,
and many possessions that were with them were lost.
And those who were in that other boat,
when they saw the disaster, returned to their house.
And the next morning the water subsided.
And men praised the unsearchable judgments of God,
and knew that the help of man is in vain.
And in this same year Danishmand died in Sebasteia,
having ruled over Melitene for two years.
And Qilij Arslan came and encamped against Melitene on the 28th of Haziran (June),
and he set up ballistas against the round tower which was in the northeast of the city.
And after fierce battles,
he captured it on the second of Ilul (September) of the year 1417,
1417 of the Greeks,
not by the sword, but by oaths (treaty).
And when he entered it and ruled over it,
he harmed no one.
And in the year five hundred of the Arabs,
while Jikirmish, the Turkish emir, was ruling over Mosul,
and was meditating rebellion against Sultan Muhammad,
the Sultan prepared another Turkish emir whose name was Jawali,
and gave him Mosul and sent him with armies.
And when Jawali reached the region of Erbil,
Jikirmish gathered his army and went and encountered him there,
and he was defeated and captured.
The people of Mosul, however, swore allegiance to the son of this Jikirmish,
whose name was Zangi,
and prepared for war with Jawali.
And they sent to Qilij Arslan, son of Sulayman, son of Qutalmish, Sultan of Iconium,
and begged him to come to their aid.
Jawali, however, came and encamped against Mosul,
with Jikirmish a prisoner with him.
And he dug a pit,
and placed him there,
because he was afraid lest the people of Mosul steal him away.
And in that pit he died.
